title: EA Capability — Establishing and Maturing the Architecture Practice

blocks.text: SESSION 1 — Concept · Key Points · Memory Technique. Read, absorb, stop.
1. Concept Explained Simply

What method do you use to build the team and function that does architecture work in the first place? The answer is elegantly self-referential: you use the ADM on itself. The EA Capability — team, tools, processes, governance — is treated as its own architecture, designed using the exact same method taught throughout this programme.

The EA practice has its own Business Architecture (governance, processes, org structure, principles), its own Data Architecture (the structure of its Enterprise Continuum and Repository — literally called "the metamodel of the architecture practice"), its own Application Architecture (the tools used to generate and govern deliverables), and its own Technology Architecture (infrastructure supporting those tools).
Establishing the practice is explicitly **not a one-off project** — it is an ongoing discipline that can trigger repeated ADM cycles as it matures.
2. Key Points
The reflexive BDAT:

headers: What it means for the EA practice itself
rows: Architecture Governance, processes, org structure, information requirements, products
The structure of the Enterprise Continuum and Architecture Repository — "the metamodel of the architecture practice"
Tools to generate, maintain, publish, distribute, and govern deliverables
Infrastructure supporting the practice's applications and Enterprise Continuum

blocks.text: Key artifacts specific to establishing the practice (mainly Phase B): Architecture Ontology (common terms/definitions) · Architecture Process (tailored ADM + governance) · Architecture Viewpoints and Views (including a specific Architecture Governance viewpoint) · Architecture Framework (deliverables, relationships, rules) · Architecture Accountability Matrix (roles and accountability) · Architecture Performance Metrics · Architecture Governance Framework.

Per-phase notes: Phase A focuses on the practice as a whole (not one project) — includes reviewing architecture practice principles (distinct from Architecture Principles) and an optional maturity assessment. Phase E focuses on organisational change, not technology selection. Phase G focuses on implementing the practice's Business Architecture — actually getting the organisation to adopt structured governance.

**Architecture Principles vs Architecture Practice Principles**: The former govern deliverables (what the target architecture must be). The latter govern the practice itself — its organisation, content, tools, process.
3. Memory Technique
"You architect the architecture practice the same way you architect anything else — apply the ADM to the EA function itself."

EXAM TRAP 1 — NOT A ONE-OFF PROJECT. Establishing the practice is an ongoing discipline, not something completed once in the Preliminary Phase. It can trigger repeated ADM cycles as the practice matures.
EXAM TRAP 2 — "DATA ARCHITECTURE" OF THE PRACTICE = ITS OWN METAMODEL. Specifically the Enterprise Continuum and Architecture Repository structure — not general business data.
EXAM TRAP 3 — ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES ≠ ARCHITECTURE PRACTICE PRINCIPLES. Different scopes: deliverables vs the practice itself. Both reviewed in Phase A.
✋ PAUSE POINT — CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING. Answer from memory before reading Session 2.
1. What is the fundamental principle behind establishing an Architecture Capability?

The ADM is used to establish the Architecture Capability — the same method used for any enterprise architecture. The EA practice is treated as an "enterprise" with its own BDAT domains. It is an ongoing discipline, not a one-off project.
2. What does "Data Architecture" mean specifically when applied to the practice itself?
The structure of the Enterprise Continuum and Architecture Repository — explicitly called "the metamodel of the architecture practice."
3. What is the difference between Architecture Principles and Architecture Practice Principles?

Architecture Principles govern the deliverables being produced. Architecture Practice Principles govern the practice itself — organisation, content, tools, process. Both reviewed in Phase A, different scopes.
SESSION 2 — Real-World Example · How It Works in Practice · Practice Questions · Part 2 Scenario
4. Real-World Example — GlobalTech Establishes Its EA Practice

**Phase A**: Scope = "establish an EA function," not "migrate to Dynamics 365." Architecture practice principles reviewed: "EA operates as a shared service"; "decisions are documented and auditable"; "mature incrementally." Maturity assessment: Level 1 (ad hoc) → target Level 3 in 18 months.

**Phase B**: Architecture Ontology (terminology tailored to business language) · Architecture Process (ADM tailored — combined steps for small initiatives) · Architecture Governance viewpoint defined for the Board · Architecture Accountability Matrix (EA Lead owns Repository, Segment Architects own Segments, Board owns governance) · Performance Metrics ("% of projects passing Compliance on first attempt").

**Phase H — the practice evolves**: The APRA regulation change (Lesson 17) triggers a new deliverable type — a Data Sovereignty Compliance Checklist — added to the Architecture Framework via Phase H of the practice's own ADM cycle, separate from the Dynamics 365 programme's cycle.
5. How It Actually Works in Practice

REALITY CHECK: MOST ORGANISATIONS IMPROVISE THEIR EA FUNCTION INSTEAD. Retroactively applying the ADM to formalise an existing informal practice is common and valuable — you don't need to have started this way to benefit from the discipline now.

REALITY CHECK: RUNNING TWO ADM CYCLES IN PARALLEL IS CONFUSING BUT ESSENTIAL. The practice's own cycle (evolving itself) and programme-specific cycles (like Dynamics 365) are separate but related. Keeping them conceptually distinct avoids confusion about which "architecture" is being discussed.
6. Part 1 Practice Questions
Q1. Which method should be used to establish an Enterprise Architecture Capability?

items: A) A dedicated EA Capability Establishment Framework, separate from the ADM
B) The same ADM used to develop any enterprise architecture — the EA practice is its own architecture ✓
C) The Architecture Governance Framework exclusively
D) An informal, ad hoc approach

blocks.text: Answer: B — the ADM is used, with the same approach as establishing any business capability.
Q2. What does the "Data Architecture" of the practice specifically refer to?

items: A) Business data used by core operational systems
B) The structure of the Enterprise Continuum and Architecture Repository — the metamodel of the practice ✓
C) Data governance policies for customer/financial data
D) The Architecture Requirements Repository only

blocks.text: Answer: B — explicitly stated in the Standard.
Q3. Which best describes the relationship between establishing an Architecture Capability and the ADM structure?

items: A) One-time activity completed within the Preliminary Phase
B) Follows the same phase-by-phase structure, is ongoing (not one-off), can trigger repeated cycles ✓
C) Bypasses the ADM entirely, uses a separate maturity model
D) Only requires Phases A and B

blocks.text: Answer: B — explicitly ongoing, not one-off.
7. Part 2 Scenario Question (Exam-Authentic Format)

SCENARIO: During Wave 2, the Architecture Board realises a new AI/ML Governance Compliance Assessment is needed for the HR module's AI recruitment screening feature. The Programme Delivery Manager says: "This is just a documentation update — let's have the EA team quickly add a checklist and move on."

rows: Agree — this is a minor administrative task, no formal process needed. Treats a change to the practice's structural framework as trivial — precisely the ungoverned drift that undermines credibility over time.

Disagree. This is a change to the practice's own Architecture Framework — a new deliverable type. Process through Phase H of the practice's own ADM cycle: classify as simplification/incremental/re-architecting; update Framework, Ontology, and Accountability Matrix; ensure governed before applying to any programme. Best answer.
Disagree — any change must always trigger a completely new ADM cycle from Phase A regardless of scale. Overly rigid, contradicts TOGAF's flexibility emphasis.

Agree it's not a big deal but require project-specific Board approval without involving the practice's broader Framework. Excludes the reusable, governed template — undermining the Framework's purpose.

blocks.text: Fold-In: TOGAF Skills Framework

When defining the Architecture Accountability Matrix (roles and accountability within the practice), the Standard points to the **TOGAF® Series Guide: Architecture Skills Framework** for guidance on the specific skills, experience, and competency levels expected of different architecture roles (e.g., Enterprise Architect, Business Architect, Data Architect, Solution Architect). It is a reference resource for structuring the EA team's capability and career development — not a separate method or deliverable type in its own right, and not required reading depth for Part 1, but useful to recognise by name if referenced in a scenario about staffing or role definition within the practice.
